mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalisation as applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based CDD screening under FICA sections 20A-28C: every proposed director, shareholder and UBO must be screened against the FIC domestic terrorist and sanctions lists, UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated sanctions list, SARB and CIPC disqualification registers. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is statutorily required for PEPs, their family members and close associates in line with FIC Guidance Note 8A; adverse hits must be escalated to the relevant accountable institution's AML Compliance Officer before any incorporation proceeds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services Portal (eservices.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A private company name must end with 'Proprietary Limited' or '(Pty) Ltd'. The name may be expressed in any of South Africa's 11 official languages; if a non-English official language is used, an English translation must be recorded in the Memorandum of Incorporation. Names in non-official languages must be transliterated into Latin script and must not consist of unintelligible sequences, offensive expressions or marks that are confusingly similar to an existing CIPC-listed name, trade mark, or protected domain name under section 11(1)-(2) and Companies Regulations 2011.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banking or Building Society (requires prior Prudential Authority/SARB approval)
Financial Services Provider (requires prior FSCA FSP licence confirmation)
Medical Scheme (requires prior Council for Medical Schemes approval)
Trust (any word implying a trust arrangement where the entity is not registered as a trust)
Any token falsely implying State, royal, cabinet, ministry or municipal association (prohibited under section 11(3))
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If CIPC rejects the name, the applicant may submit a formal reconsideration request via the CIPC e-Services portal within 15 business days of the rejection notice, attaching legal argument on compliance with section 11(2) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and the Companies Regulations 2011. If the reconsideration is refused, the applicant may apply to the Companies Tribunal for a section 11(5) review within 30 days, and thereafter appeal to the High Court. A successful reservation is valid for 24 months, and a single extension of up to 12 months may be requested before expiry upon payment of the prescribed CIPC tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible under section 23(1) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 only if the virtual/serviced office provides a physical address, not a post-office box, that is capable of receiving legal process and official correspondence. Such arrangements are accepted by CIPC, but for an IP HoldCo using ISIC 6420 the absence of local staff, records and substance materially elevates shell-company red flags under FICA section 21E and may trigger enhanced due diligence by banks and corporate service providers.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-Elevated: estimated annualised probability of 10-15% for a passive IP HoldCo using a virtual office and relying on cross-border royalty flows; CIPC, FIC and SARS conduct unannounced physical inspections at the registered office, and the probability rises if tax authority risk indicators flag non-resident royalty payments without demonstrated commercial substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008 (as amended), sections 13, 14, 19, 39, 66, 70; Companies Regulations, 2011
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) and Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; at least one share must be issued and fully paid. Foreign shareholder contributions are subject to SARB exchange-control reporting; no escrow deposit is required under the Companies Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that: 1. The subscribers listed in the Memorandum of Incorporation do hereby subscribe for and take up the initial shares, paid in full, in accordance with section 39 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. 2. The registered office of the company shall be at [Physical Address] within the Republic of South Africa, as recorded on the Notice of Incorporation. 3. The following persons are appointed as first directors: [Names] and [Names], respectively, each serving until replaced by a shareholders' resolution. 4. The board authorizes the directors jointly and severally to execute all documents, open bank accounts, and make regulatory filings necessary to commence the company's business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) — e-Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to CIPC e-Services, select 'Register a Company' and file a Name Reservation application (CoR 9.1). Pay the applicable fee. The reserved name remains valid for six months.
required_dossiers: Applicant's certified identity document and proof of authority
Power of attorney where filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a fresh application with an alternate name or launch an objection within 30 days of the CIPC notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Notice of Incorporation and MOI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) and have it signed by the incorporators. Submit the CoR 14.1 Notice of Incorporation together with the signed MOI via CIPC e-Services. Pay the registration fee and await the registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of incorporators, directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend any flagged provisions in line with CIPC commentary and resubmit within the prescribed 20-business-day period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Tax and Statutory Levies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After CIPC registration, register the company on SARS efiling for income tax, VAT, PAYE and UIF/SDL as applicable. Submit the requisite forms and obtain the income tax reference number and tax compliance status.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to SARS supporting-document requests and reconcile company registration details within 10 business days to avoid penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Governance Structure and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / CIPC Records Update
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting and adopt the resolution approving share subscription, appointment of directors, company secretary and registered office address. File any alterations to company records with CIPC.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease or title deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC rejects the particulars filing, correct the registered-office proof and resubmit with the company's supporting documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Bank Account and Secure Operational Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Dealer Bank / South African Reserve Bank (SARB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account at an authorized dealer using certified company documents. For foreign inbound capital, submit a Form JI through the bank to the SARB Financial Surveillance Department. In parallel, obtain a fire safety certificate for the registered office if it hosts employees or assets.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Incorporation and board resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries beneficial ownership, provide a completed BO register and corrected identity documents.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (dtic) and Department of Employment and Labour
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificate of Good Standing (CIPC) and COIDA Letter of Good Standing (if employees are engaged)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt under NEMA EIA Regulations Listing Notices 1–3 (2014) — no listed activities for pure IP licensing
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharges; comply with municipal waste management by-laws and the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008 for office waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the local municipal fire authority; compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 including structural safety, emergency planning, and first-aid availability at the registered premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS), via the SARS eFiling portal at www.sars.gov.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated entity must first register as a 'foreign resident' taxpayer with SARS by completing the non-resident taxpayer registration process and obtaining an income tax reference number. If the entity makes taxable supplies in South Africa or is required to account for VAT, it must separately apply for VAT registration under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, on Form VAT 101 (or electronically via eFiling). Applicants must submit constitutional documents, proof of foreign registration, SARS corporate registration details, and the physical address of the South African representative or place of business.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a check-the-box classification regime. Statutory elections are limited, including VAT grouping under section 50 of the VAT Act, group taxation relief under the Income Tax Act, and transfer-pricing considerations. Hybrid mismatch rules are largely mandatory and apply via sections 8E, 8EA, 8F, 8FA, 8J, 9D and related provisions, with no elective hybrid-mismatch avoidance mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991 (South African VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration threshold: ZAR 1,000,000 in taxable supplies in any 12-month period; voluntary registration threshold: ZAR 50,000; foreign suppliers of electronic services must register when total taxable supplies to South African recipients exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SARS requires registered vendors to issue full tax invoices in compliance with section 20 of the VAT Act, with prescribed particulars including vendor VAT number, invoice number, date, customer identity, description, quantity, price and VAT amount. SARS is implementing an eInvoicing framework aligned to international standards, but there is no real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory digital stamping currently in force. Certain high- and medium-risk vendors have electronic data submission obligations to SARS through the eFiling and data reporting channels, including VAT information verification (VIV) processes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating is available for exported goods when physical export is shipped out of South Africa within the prescribed period and documentary proof is retained. For services and intellectual property, zero rating may apply under section 11(2)(l) of the VAT Act where the supply is made to a non-resident and the services or rights are for the direct benefit or direct use of the non-resident outside South Africa. A patent licensing royalty derived by a South African IP HoldCo from a foreign licensee can qualify for zero rating if the licensed intellectual property is exploited outside South Africa and the supplier holds adequate substantiation, including proof of the non-resident status of the customer and the foreign use or benefit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: SARS Customs Export Declaration (SAD 500) for physical goods
Signed international sales or licensing agreement
Commercial invoice and packing list (for goods)
Bill of lading or airway bill / proof of physical export
Inward remittance certificate or SWIFT / FEC proof of payment in foreign currency
Documentary evidence of non-resident status of the foreign customer
Retained records showing the foreign direct benefit or foreign exploitation of the licensed intellectual property
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may conduct forensic audits of zero-rated export and royalty transactions, requiring production of full documentary evidence. If zero rating is incorrectly claimed, SARS will raise an additional assessment for VAT at 15%, plus interest and a penalty under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011. Understatement penalties may range from 10% up to 200% of the tax shortfall depending on culpability. Where fraudulent intent is established, criminal prosecution may follow under Section 235 of the Tax Administration Act and Section 17 of the VAT Act, with potential fines and imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through its Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) as the Exchange Control Authority, with the Prudential Authority for banking supervision and the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) for AML/CFT oversight; National Treasury exercises policy oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand (ZAR) is a non-internationalised controlled currency. Current account transactions, including royalty receipts and outbound IP licence payments, are freely convertible through Authorised Dealers (ADs) under the Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers, subject to verification, documentation, and reporting. Capital account flows, such as inbound equity subscription and intercompany shareholder loans to a South African resident IP HoldCo, require prior AD 'no objection' or SARB FinSurv approval where the transaction exceeds AD delegated limits. Profit remittance by dividend is permissible without SARB approval where paid from taxed distributable reserves, supported by a dividend declaration and SARB Form MP37/MPC-185, with the AD effecting conversion. Royalty payments to non-resident licensors are permitted under Exchange Control Regulation 10(1)(c) provided the underlying licence agreement is approved by or warranted to the AD and SARS tax compliance verification is satisfied. No material current-account conversion hurdles exist for a documented IP patent licensing treasury, but meticulous purpose code filing and documentary retention are mandatory.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: South Africa abolished mandatory surrender/conversion of export proceeds on 1 October 1996. However, all export proceeds, including royalty income earned by a South African IP licensor from foreign licensees, must be repatriated to South Africa within 180 days of the due date or date of invoice, whichever is earlier, under the Currency and Exchanges Manual (export proceeds repatriation rule). Repatriated proceeds may either be converted to ZAR on the spot market or deposited into a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) held with an Authorised Dealer, which may be retained without conversion. The AD must be supplied with a Form FX or electronic matching of the export/royalty invoice, and late repatriation without a SARB-approved extension constitutes an exchange control offence.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (ZAR) with linked Foreign Currency Account for royalty receipts and IP sub-licence collections
Operational Account (ZAR) with Capital Escrow sub-account for inbound equity injection compliance
Operational Account (ZAR) with dedicated Escrow Account for licence fee clearing and dividend distributions
Operational Account (ZAR) and Export Proceeds Foreign Currency Account for outbound FX hedging
Operational Account (ZAR) with specialised Wealth/Corporate Treasury overlay

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium feasibility for a South African resident IP HoldCo. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Currencycloud-type platforms) cannot lawfully hold ZAR operational accounts for a South African resident without being registered as an Authorised Dealer or partnering with a domestic AD; their use as a treasury centre triggers Exchange Control Regulation 10 and FICA non-compliance. An EMIs role is limited to inbound collection origination outside South Africa, with onward routing via SWIFT MT103 to the domestic AD account. A locally licensed fintech (e.g., a registered payment service provider under the National Payment System Act) may offer segregated operational rails but does not replace the AD corporate banking relationship required for royalty remittances, capital injections, and SARB reporting. The AD banking hub remains mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA) and the 2023 EDD/CDD Rules, a legal person is verified through its Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) registration, Memorandum of Incorporation, board resolution authorising account opening, and the identification of all directors and beneficial owners. Physical presence of directors is institutionally preferred but not statutorily absolute: all tier-1 banks permit remote onboarding with notarised/apostilled certified copies of IDs and proof of residential address, supplemented by a biometric-verified video KYC interview with the Relationship Manager and Compliance Officer. In practice, banks require at least one director or authorised signatory to hold a valid SARS tax reference number and, for a Medium-Risk Enhanced IP HoldCo, an in-person or high-assurance virtual interview is mandated before issuance of the Authorised Dealer mandate. Non-resident directors must provide sworn affidavits, apostilled passport copies, and independent professional references to permit remote signing without physical branch attendance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Thin-capitalised IP HoldCo with non-resident parent and high-value cross-border royalty flows, classified Medium-Risk Enhanced; UBO opacity at CIPC register.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate structure chart, share register and beneficial ownership register filed with CIPC, board resolutions, certified MOI, source-of-wealth letters for all inbound capital, parent company audited financials for 3 years, and a written treasury rationale for the South African licensing function.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transfer pricing and tax avoidance red flags on outbound royalty rates and intercompany licensing to low-tax jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OECD-aligned transfer pricing policy under s.31 of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962, including Master File and Local File, arm's-length royalty benchmarking study, patent/trademark registration evidence (PCT, ARIPO, UKIPO, EUIPO), licence negotiation memoranda, and substance documentation (South African board minutes, local premises, key management payroll, economic substance assessment).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious fund flows: mismatched invoice narratives, rapid in-and-out movements, or round-tripping through multiple intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed global IP licence and sub-licence agreements, three-way matched bank statements, invoicing and pricing schedules, foreign licensee confirmation of services/receipt, transaction flow charts per contract, and an independent forensic accountant's opinion on economic purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP, sanctions, or adverse media hits on non-resident UBOs or licensee counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening results across UN, EU, OFAC, UK HMT, and consolidated FIC lists, PEP declarations, negative news search reports, source-of-funds evidence for any PEP-linked investment, and a legal opinion from an external counsel confirming the permissibility of the relationship under FICA and international sanctions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SARS tax compliance mismatch: outstanding income tax or VAT returns, or absence of valid tax compliance status at onboarding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid SARS tax compliance status pin, filed ITR14 and VAT201 returns, proof of provisional tax payments, royalty revenue ledger segmented by licensee, and, where applicable, an advance transfer pricing agreement or unilateral APA application letter.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for inbound equity or shareholder loan funding into the South African IP HoldCo: (i) submit a boarding pack to the AD comprising board and shareholder resolutions, executed subscription or loan agreement, source-of-funds evidence, and the FICA-complete KYC file; (ii) obtain the AD's 'no objection' or rely on the AD's delegated approval where the inward amount falls within the SARB FinSurv delegated limits for inward foreign investments; (iii) execute the wire via SWIFT MT103 with an appropriate purpose code derived from the Currency and Exchanges Manual (equity subscription: Capital/Equity code; shareholder loan: Intercompany Loan code) and populate field 72 with the agreement reference; (iv) upon receipt, reconcile the inward foreign exchange against the AD's Form BF inward transfer record and retain an inward investment certificate or AD confirmation for the treasury file; (v) ensure the beneficiary reference excludes vague language and instead states the SARB purpose code, invoice or agreement number, and the licensing commercial segment to avoid AML scoring anomalies. For capital injections exceeding AD delegated limits, a formal SARB FinSurv application must precede remittance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for outbound trade and IP disbursements are ranked as follows: (1) SWIFT MT103 for royalty, sub-licence fee, and intercompany IP service payments to foreign beneficiaries, sent only through the AD and backed by a finance pack of invoice, executed licence agreement, royalty calculation schedule, SARS tax compliance status, and, where required, the AD or FinSurv approval letter; (2) SWIFT MT202 COV for treasury internal house transfers between the South African AD hub and offshore foreign currency accounts or for correspondent clearing of larger aggregated disbursements; (3) Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700) where the IP licence is bundled with goods or technology-hardware trade, with documents negotiated via the Rand clearing mechanism and SAMOS settlement; (4) domestic rails (SAMOS RTGS and the local settlement system) for ZAR payments to South African counterparties such as service providers, refunds, or security deposits. All outbound MT103 payments must include the correct exchange control purpose code, and the supporting electronic evidence must be retained for at least five years under FIC Section 27A obligations; the AD performs exchange control vetting on each instruction against Regulation 10 and the licensed mandate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward exchange contracts (FECs) entered into with an Authorised Dealer to hedge forecast royalty receipts or payable obligations in USD, EUR, or GBP, with tenors up to 12 months standard and longer tenors subject to SARB FinSurv approval
Purchased currency options (over-the-counter) from an AD, permitting upside participation and downside protection on licence fee exposures, with no naked option writing by the corporate treasury

Cross-currency swaps commenced on-balance-sheet, matched to underlying intercompany licence cash flows, with SARB FinSurv notification where the swap tenor or notional exceeds the AD's delegated authority

Offshore ZAR non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) arranged on a back-to-back basis through an AD or its offshore affiliate, strictly supported by an evidenced underlying commercial royalty exposure; speculative NDF positioning is prohibited for South African residents
Exchange-traded listed currency futures and options on approved local or offshore exchanges subject to an AD-approved corporate hedging mandate and SARB liquidity reporting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form CoR 28.1; includes Public Interest Score declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation; financial year-end is not the reference date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late lodgement incurs escalating penalties of approximately USD 6 to USD 56 per month depending on delay; continued non-compliance triggers a final deregistration notice and administrative strike-off from the companies register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Filing (Form CoR 30.1 linked to Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, filed concurrently with the Annual Return; any shareholding or beneficial interest change must also be updated within 10 business days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the beneficial ownership declaration renders the company suspected of committing an offence under the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; sanctions include administrative fines up to USD 14,000 and criminal liability for directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) approval, signature, and retention; audited/reviewed copy filed only if Public Interest Score (PIS) thresholds or regulatory conditions require
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC (filing conditionally required) and SARS (retained with tax records)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AFS must be prepared and approved by the board within 6 months after financial year-end; if audited or independently reviewed, the report must be completed within the same 6-month window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC compliance notice with administrative penalty up to USD 2,800 for repeated default; directors jointly and severally liable for loss if AFS are defective or withheld from members.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A full independent audit is compulsory if the Public Interest Score exceeds 500; a score between 350 and 500 requires an audit unless an independent review is elected; a score from 100 to 349 requires an independent review; a score below 100 requires no audit or review, though IFRS financial statements must still be prepared and stored.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB for larger entities; IFRS for SMEs (adopted by the South African Institute of Chartered Accountants and CIPC) may be used by this Proprietary Limited IP Holding Company if it meets the small- and medium-sized entity criteria; no alternative local GAAP is permitted for companies required to produce AFS under the Companies Act 71 of 2008.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register (Form CoR 30.1 schedule) detailing each individual with 5% or more beneficial interest, control through voting rights, or ability to appoint directors; this register must be filed with CIPC on each Annual Return and updated whenever transfer of shares alters beneficial ownership.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and share transfer register (including previous secretary's share certificates)
Register of Directors and prescribed officers
Register of Beneficial Owners (Form CoR 30.1 schedules)
Minute Book of members' and directors' resolutions
Financial records ledger, general journal, and supporting transfer documents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120 to USD 600 per annum for Corporate Secretarial or Registered Office services in South Africa
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800 to USD 5,500 per annum for an independent review or audit of a single-shareholder IP licensing HoldCo with moderate intercompany royalty flow; full IFRS audit may extend to USD 8,000 if the PIS is elevated.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for tax years of assessment commencing on or after 1 April 2022
